texts.facts: In all these matters, the applicants have prayed that the First Information Reports registered for the offence 179, 188, 328 of the Indian Penal Code (IPC) read with Section 59 (iii) of the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006 (in short "the Act of 2006") be [LEAKAGE_MASK]. The main thrust of challenge is that the allegation in the FIR does not spell out offence under the provisions of the Act of 2006 and Rules framed under it and consequently offence under section of the IPC is not made out. 2. By order dated 31.10.2014, the present application along with connected matters was admitted and interim order granted earlier was confirmed. It is submitted that the issue involved in the present application is covered by the said judgment. The non-applicant no. 1 has filed reply and submitted that registration of the FIR under Section 328 of the IPC cannot be faulted, as the material on record fulfills ingredients of Section 328 of the IPC. [2018 AIR (SC) 5348] and submitted that it is open for the Food Safety Officer to independently filed complaint before the Competent Court for the offence under provision of the Act of 2006. The learned A.P.P. further submitted that the investigation in all the matters is completed and charge-sheets are ready.
texts.arguments: It is also submitted by Shri R. L. Khapre, learned Senior Advocate that from the averments in the FIR, ingredients of the offence alleged against the applicants are not fulfilled. Haq is a party) and submitted that similar order be passed in the present applications as facts of these batch of applications are similar.
